summary: The dice entity page covers CanonicalDice, something a person rolls, made once and used anywhere. It is one kind with three types, a roll, a table or a pool, and each carries only the field its type rolls. Rolling itself is not a piece but math in src/core/dice.ts, the same module the roll macro, the battle tracker and the spellbook use, while rollDicePiece in src/core/dice-piece.ts says what each type rolls on randomness the caller hands in. The page lists the types with example results, says a tool links a dice piece by id so a model can roll it with the turn's seeded randomness, gives the rules checked when a piece is saved, and notes that the editor waits for its wireframe while New dice saves a blank 1d20 roll.

sections.title: Types
sections.summary: A roll carries dice, notation such as 2d6 or 1d20+3, and totals it, answering with the piece's name, the notation, each die, the modifier and the total. A table carries rows, of at least one, each a text and a whole weight of one or more; it rolls one die the size of all the weights together and lands on the row that number falls in, so a row of weight two is twice as likely as a row of weight one. A pool carries a count of dice, their sides of two or more, and a target; each die at or over the target counts as a success, and the answer lists the dice and the number of successes. A roll is never refused or shortened for being big: the answer lists each die up to twenty dice, then gives the count, lowest, highest and total, and the trace keeps every die.

sections.title: Where dice are used
sections.summary: A tool links a dice piece by its id through the tool's dice action, described on the tool page, so a model writing a reply can call that tool and roll the piece. The roll is decided by the turn's seeded randomness, which means the same seed rolls the same result. This is the one place the page names where dice pieces are used today: a dice piece is made once in the Library and any number of tools can link it, instead of each tool carrying its own fixed dice notation. The page does not describe any other host, such as a scene or a promptbook, using dice pieces directly yet.

sections.title: The rules
sections.summary: A piece carries exactly the field its type rolls and no other field: a roll carries dice, a table carries rows, and a pool carries pool. A roll's dice must be readable notation with at least one die of at least two sides, and a pool's target may not be greater than its number of sides. All of these rules are checked when the piece is saved, by the dice kind's strict decoder, so a stored piece can always be rolled and never fails at the moment a tool or anything else asks it for a result. The only other bounds are hostile-input ceilings, set about a hundred times past real use and refused as unusually large, not design limits.

sections.title: Editing
sections.summary: There is no editor for dice pieces yet. The dice editor waits for its approved wireframe, so no screen for editing a roll, a table or a pool exists in this change. The Library's New dice action saves a blank piece, a roll of 1d20, which is a valid stored piece under the rules above and can be linked from a tool as it is. The section records the missing editor as a known gap rather than describing a surface that is not built, and promises nothing about the editor beyond the wireframe that must be approved first, in the same way the tool page treats its own missing editor.
